title: Prelude blob not invalidated by a change to an intrinsic's hand-written STG wrapper
description: Observed while fault-injecting eu-oaz72.124 (PR #1321). Editing the wrapper of seqListThen in src/eval/stg/force.rs (to λ{2} ✳1) and rebuilding: `eu dump runtime` showed the edited wrapper, but in blob mode execution kept the old behaviour (the list elements were still forced); --source-prelude showed the new behaviour. build.rs reported the blob fresh, because the blob hash covers lib/prelude.eu, src/eval/intrinsics.rs and the DEMAND_ANALYSIS_PATHS list in src/eval/stg/wire_format.rs, but not the wrapper sources under src/eval/stg/. Effect: a local fault injection or wrapper fix silently does not take effect in blob mode until `cargo xtask prelude-compile` is rerun, so a harness test can look like it fails to gate. CI compiles the blob fresh (it is git-ignored), so CI is not affected. Fix to consider: include the intrinsic wrapper sources in the blob hash, or document that a wrapper change needs prelude-compile. Not yet explained: an edit to the DICT.MERGE_WITH_STRICT wrapper in src/eval/stg/dict.rs did take effect without recompiling.

title: dict: native merge-with-strict (prelude fold is 7.6 s vs 4.5 s lazy, stack grows with b)
description: From eu-oaz72.21 (PR #1191); see docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-13-dict-ordered-ops-benchmarks.md. dict.merge-with-strict is a prelude fold: 7.6 s against 4.5 s for lazy merge-with, and its stack grows with the size of b. Make it a native intrinsic (same names and behaviour; no API change). Performance work: follow eucalypt-performance; measured figures under the protocol.
close_reason: Merged in PR #1321 (merge commit ab294f7): dict.merge-with-strict is now the native DICT.MERGE_WITH_STRICT intrinsic with seqListThen, constant stack, same evaluation order as the old fold.
